meta.homeTitle: Hoosat Create · React SSR without the framework
meta.homeDescription: Scaffold a full-stack React 19 and TypeScript app that streams server-rendered HTML from a small, Express-free Node.js server. One command: npx hoosat-create@latest.
meta.tutorialTitle: Tutorial · Build and ship a site with Hoosat Create
meta.tutorialDescription: Step-by-step guide from an empty folder to a deployed, server-rendered React site with Hoosat Create. The same steps built create.hoosat.fi.

hero.lead: Hoosat Create scaffolds a full-stack React and TypeScript app that streams HTML from a small, dependency-light Node.js server. No Express, no magic, just code you can read and own.

command.label: command to a running SSR app

speed.title: Measured on your visit
speed.lead: Fast is easy to claim, so here are the numbers. They are measured live in your browser for the page load that opened this site, from the Server-Timing header this server sends and the browser's own timing APIs.

server.label: Server render
server.hint: Routing the request to the first byte of streamed HTML

interactive.label: Interactive
interactive.hint: React finished hydrating the server HTML

separation.title: Client and server, kept apart
separation.lead: Many React frameworks fuse server and client code into the same files with server components, loaders and server actions, and decide at build time what runs where. In Hoosat Create, the folder decides.

client.body: Your React app: pages, components and CSS. Bundled for the browser, starting from src/client/index.tsx.

server.body: Your own HTTP server: middlewares, API routes and rendering. Bundled into build/server.js, starting from src/server/index.tsx.

common.body: Code both sides import, like this site's language picker and settings. Nothing browser- or server-specific.

separation.note: Two webpack configs, two bundles and no "use client" or "use server" directives. You always know what ships to the browser.

features.title: Everything a production site needs, nothing it doesn't
features.lead: The template is a starting point you copy, not a framework you depend on. Every feature below is plain code in your repository.

ssr.title: Streaming SSR
ssr.body: Pages render with React 19's renderToPipeableStream, so the browser gets real HTML first and then hydrates it into an interactive app.

router.title: A router you can read
router.body: The server core is a few hundred lines of TypeScript on Node's http and https modules: middlewares, :params, wildcards and composable routers.

seo.title: SEO in the first bytes
seo.body: Titles, meta, Open Graph and JSON-LD written with react-helmet-async are streamed into the head, so crawlers see them without running JavaScript.

compression.title: Precompressed assets
compression.body: The build writes Brotli, gzip and deflate copies of every public file. The server picks one by Accept-Encoding and sets long cache headers.

typescript.title: TypeScript everywhere
typescript.body: Strict TypeScript 6 for client, server and shared code. Even the build tools are .ts files that Node runs directly with type stripping.

i18n.title: Built-in i18n
i18n.body: i18next and react-i18next are wired in on both sides. This site renders English or Finnish per request. Try the switch in the header.

security.title: Secure defaults
security.body: A Content-Security-Policy header with a nonce, path traversal safe static files, and an .npmrc that only installs packages public for 7 days.

testing.title: Tests from day one
testing.body: Jest 30 and Testing Library come configured, with example tests for the server core. Run npm test and npm run typecheck in CI.

dev.title: Fast dev loop
dev.body: npm run dev rebuilds the client and the server whenever you save and restarts the server with nodemon, so changes show up in seconds.

flow.title: How a request becomes a page
flow.lead: One request through the stack, from socket to interactive page. Each step is a file you can open.

request.title: Request
request.body: Node's http or https server accepts the request, and the URL is sanitised against path traversal.

middleware.title: Middlewares
middleware.body: Middlewares run in order. On this site: robots.txt and sitemap.xml, then precompressed static files.

route.title: Routes
route.body: API routes such as /api/ping/:id answer directly. Everything else falls through to the * route.

render.title: React render
render.body: The * route picks the language, renders <App /> inside a StaticRouter and streams it to the client.

head.title: Head injection
head.body: A transform stream writes Helmet tags, preload links and the bundles into the head while the HTML streams out.

hydrate.title: Hydration
hydrate.body: In the browser hydrateRoot attaches React to the existing markup. From here on, navigation happens on the client.

code.title: Your server is just a file
code.lead: src/server/index.tsx is the whole server. Middlewares and routes are plain functions. This is a trimmed version of the file that serves this page.

stack.title: Current, boring, supported
stack.lead: Every dependency is on its latest major release, and the template is tested on all supported Node.js LTS lines.

demo.title: Talk to the server
demo.lead: This button calls the /api/ping route from src/server/api-routes. The page itself was rendered on the server: turn JavaScript off and reload, it still reads the same.
demo.resultServer: Server replied “{{reply}}”: {{server}} ms on the server, {{ms}} ms round trip.
demo.noscript: With JavaScript off, the button opens the API's reply directly.

cta.title: Start your next site in one command
cta.lead: Run the command, answer a few questions and open http://localhost:8181. The tutorial walks you through the rest.

tutorial.title: Build and ship a site with Hoosat Create
tutorial.lead: This walkthrough takes you from an empty folder to a deployed, server-rendered React site. It is exactly how create.hoosat.fi was made, and every code sample comes from its source.
tutorial.source: View the full source on GitHub

prereq.title: Before you start
prereq.p1: You need Node.js 22, 24 or 26 and git. Check your versions:
prereq.p2: Older Node.js versions can not run the build tools, which are TypeScript files executed directly by Node.

create.title: Create the project
create.p1: Run the generator and answer its questions, or pass the answers as arguments:
create.p2: The script clones `hoosat-template` with the `hoosat-server-core` submodule, writes your details into `package.json`, runs `npm install` and can initialise a git repository for you.

dev.title: Start the dev server
dev.p1: `npm run dev` builds into `build-dev`, starts the server and rebuilds whenever you save a file in `src` or `public`.
dev.p2: Open `http://localhost:8181`. The port comes from `PORT` in `.env`.

layout.title: Find your way around
layout.p1: Everything lives in `src`, split by where the code runs. Client and server code are never mixed in the same file, so the folder tells you what ends up in the browser:
layout.p2: `src/server/core` is a git submodule shared by every Hoosat project. Update it with `git submodule update --remote` instead of editing it in place.

page.title: Add a page
page.p1: Pages are ordinary React components. Create one under `src/client/routes`:
page.p2: Then add it to the route list in `src/client/App.tsx`. The browser router and the server share that list, and the server uses it to answer unknown URLs with a real 404 status.

api.title: Add an API route
api.p1: API routes use the core router. Create a router, add handlers and mount it in `src/server/api-routes/index.ts`:
api.p2: Path parameters are in `req.params`, and `res.status()`, `res.send()` and `res.json()` cover most responses.

seo.title: Set titles and meta tags
seo.p1: Put head tags inside `<Helmet>` anywhere in a page. On the server the renderer streams them into `<head>` before the body, so search engines and link previews see them without JavaScript.
seo.p2: This site keeps all of it in one `Seo` component that also writes the canonical URL, Open Graph and JSON-LD tags.

style.title: Style it
style.p1: Drop plain `.css` files anywhere under `src/client`. The build merges and minifies them into `/public/styles.css`, which the renderer links in every page. No imports needed.
style.p2: This site defines its colours as CSS custom properties, so dark and light mode are one media query.

i18n.title: Translate it
i18n.p1: The template ships i18next on both sides. This site picks the language per request, from a cookie or the `Accept-Language` header:
i18n.p2: Translations are bundled and initialised synchronously, so the server and the browser produce identical markup and hydration never flashes untranslated keys.

test.title: Test it
test.p1: Tests live in `src/__tests__` and run with Jest. Type check the whole project separately:
test.p2: This site's tests cover the language picker, the sitemap, the 404 handling, a full server render and that both languages have the same keys.

deploy.title: Build and deploy
deploy.p1: `npm run build` writes a production build into `build`, including precompressed copies of every asset. Webpack bundles the server and its dependencies into `build/server.js`, so production only needs that folder:
deploy.p2: Put the server behind a reverse proxy such as Caddy or nginx for TLS, or run it as a container with the Dockerfile in the repository:
deploy.p3: That's it: a server-rendered React site in production, built from code you understand.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: This URL doesn't exist, and the server said so with a real 404 status code, not a soft 200.
